narrative.overview:
A pale blue work surface, deep navy ink and cobalt actions make a small, practical document tool. Public Sans provides the same readable voice for controls and document text. Ruled white panels distinguish tools from evidence without ornamental depth.

This record derives from the phase 2 implementation and its desktop library, mobile library and native-PDF renders. The code-led visual direction is provisional: no user-approved comp or established brand assets exist. The library extends the same inspection desk; future capabilities must not be inferred from it.
keyCharacteristics: A cool, lightly tinted ground surrounding white working surfaces.
Cobalt for actions and active evidence state.
One readable sans-serif family with a restrained hierarchy.
Fine dividers and softened corners instead of shadows.

rules.name: The Action Color Rule
rules.body: Cobalt identifies an action or active state; reading surfaces remain neutral.

rules.name: The Single Voice Rule
rules.body: Use Public Sans for interface and plain-text evidence; establish hierarchy through size, weight and spacing.

rules.name: The Ruled Surface Rule
rules.body: Distinguish adjacent working regions with tonal surfaces and fine dividers before adding depth.

dos: Do use cobalt for actions and active state, with neutral reading surfaces.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus and reduced-motion behavior.
Do use fine dividers and tone to distinguish working regions.
Do keep original document content readable and show partial or failed previews explicitly.
donts: Don't substitute glyph characters for the implemented SVG icons.
Don't inherit browser PDF toolbar colors, icons or typography as application tokens.
Don't turn this surface's first viewport or future product phases into global visual requirements.
